newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends higher in lacklustre trade.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends higher in lacklustre trade.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar closed slightly higher against its U.S. counterpart as recent hectic quarter-end demand for the greenback slowed during the abbreviated Saturday session, dealers said.
The local unit traded within a narrow range before closing at T$27.902 against Friday's T$27.913 finish.
Turnover through dealers was a modest US$104 million.
Dealers said buying sentiment for the U.S. dollar was dampened further by the central bank's strong defence on behalf of the local currency on Friday.
"By intervening, the central bank was making clear that it did not want to see the Taiwan dollar depreciate too fast in the near future," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
"Market sentiment also is typically lacklustre on a Saturday," she added.
Dealers said they expected the rate to consolidate around the T$27.9 level in the near term.
A T$27.88-92 range was seen for Monday.
